name: clawrium
description: CLI fleet management for AI agents on local networks - deploy, upgrade, and monitor OpenClaw/ZeroClaw/IronClaw across hosts via Ansible

paragraphs: Fleet management for AI agents on your local network.

You're running multiple AI agents - coding assistants, internal tools, experiment harnesses - across machines on your network. Without Clawrium, you SSH into each box, manage configs individually, lose track of token spend, and have no unified view of what's running where.
Clawrium gives you kubectl-style fleet control for AI agents:
features: One CLI, all hosts. Add machines to your fleet and deploy any agent type to any host.

Specialized agents. Each agent does one job and does it well. Instead of one overloaded assistant, run a fleet of purpose-built agents - a coding agent, a review agent, a research agent - each with its own context,…

Local inference. Use hardware you already have - Mac Minis, NVIDIA DGX Spark, spare servers - as inference providers. Run smaller open models like Gemma, GPT-4o-mini, Kimi, or Llama locally and point multiple agents at…
Model experimentation. Swap models across agents to compare performance without touching individual configs.
Lifecycle management. Upgrades, rollbacks, secrets rotation, backups - handled.

whatItDoes.text: Fleet management for AI agents on your local network.

requirements.text: There's no dashboard, no SaaS, no account signup.
On macOS hosts you must enable Remote Login before registering them; see docs/host-preparation.md.
